topics.topic: Action-specific data and mechanisms required to reproduce retention actions after restore
questions: How is an audit-entry erasure represented in the retention-review record when it has no `customer_ref` or `project_id`?
If the backup contains an active project that was later archived and erased, how may the owner reproduce the erasure after restore?
Which action-specific inputs must the retention-review record preserve so the owner can reproduce the intended restored state without guessing?
Must the retained import choices also include all Customer mapping values required by A16, and if not, where do those values come from after a restore?

quotes:
What the owner repeats after a restore — erasures,
restrictions, ends of a relationship, the latest date audit entries were
erased by — follows the owner's record of the retention review (R0-60): a
governance document, outside this case (Explicit exclusions), naming each
action by its date, kind and the `customer_ref` or `project_id` it touched,
with no personal value.

The owner first starts the restored instance owner-only (A17 rule 1), so
no service and no agent reaches it, and brings each Customer and project to
the state the owner's own record of the retention review (R0-60) gives for
it now — erased, restricted, ended or not — and erases audit entries before
the latest date the owner erased by, before configuring the tokens and
starting it again.
unknown or active project refused; anonymising an anonymised project returns it unchanged, and deleting it whole is refused (R0-71)

A store lost before a checked backup holds the import
loses the import with it, and the import may then be made again: the owner
keeps the export file and the picks, names and aliases given in the import
until a checked backup holds the import, and retires the VPS instance only
then (R0-79).
judgement.divergence: One implementation preserves and replays prerequisite archives, effective relationship-end dates, audit cutoffs, and every Customer import-mapping value; another preserves only the listed date, kind, subject id, picks, names and aliases, so it must refuse, guess, or produce a different restored state. The owner and every caller reading the restored Registry notice the difference.
judgement.why: The recovery rules require exact reconstruction but omit action-specific inputs and prerequisites needed to perform it.

topics.topic: Canonical encoding and digest computation for confirmation-bound inputs
questions: What exact ordered byte representation is hashed when binding a confirmation to its inputs, including absent values, collections, text and import picks?
How are an action, target, version and inputs converted into the confirmation-binding digest so every implementation compares the same values?
How are confirmation-bound values canonically encoded and digested so every implementation decides equality identically?

judgement.why: This is the same canonical confirmation-binding encoding and digest question already assigned to State 6.

precedent.topic: Canonical encoding and digest for confirmation-bound inputs
quotes:
kept as a digest of those values in a fixed order, never
   as the values themselves; a submission's inputs are bound when their digest
   equals it.
precedent.why: The canonical byte encoding, field order, digest algorithm and representation of absent values are encoding and contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Canonical identity and digest computation for import files
questions: How exactly is the import file digest calculated and compared?
What exact value identifies an import file for confirmation, the migration closure and the audit entry?
What exact computation defines equality and identity of an uploaded import file?

judgement.why: This is the same import-file digest algorithm and canonical input-representation question already assigned to State 6.

precedent.topic: Import-file digest algorithm, input representation, comparison, and collisions
quotes: The mapping names the file by its digest.
What Registry defines is the file it accepts on import; its format belongs to States 5 and 6.
precedent.why: The digest algorithm, canonical byte representation and encoded digest form are format and contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Handling an expired pending confirmation when a different value is submitted
questions: When the pending confirmation has expired and the submission gives a different value, is the pending confirmation cleared or retained?
If the pending confirmation has expired and a submission supplies a different value, is the expired pending confirmation cleared or retained?
When the pending confirmation has expired and the submission gives a different value, is the expired pending confirmation cleared or retained?

quotes:
It is valid only in that session, while
   less than 10 minutes have passed since it was shown — an expired one is
   refused and cleared by any submission that reaches the confirmation check,
   whatever value it gives — and is used up by the first submission that carries it, whatever
   its answer; a refused submission needs the step shown again.

A submission
   carries it when it passes the owner session and CSRF checks (A04 rule 6,
   stage 1) and gives a value equal to the pending one; from there on,
   whatever the answer — a binding to another action or input included — the
   pending value is used up. A submission refused before those checks, or
   giving another value, is refused and leaves the pending value as it was.
judgement.why: The first passage clears an expired confirmation regardless of the submitted value, while the second retains it when the submitted value differs.

topics.topic: Recovery and reported outcome when backup status metadata is missing, inconsistent, or unwritable
questions: After a crash between publishing a checked backup and updating the status file, which outcome must the owner interface show and does that day count as having a backup?
What does Registry do at start when kept backups exist but the status file cannot be read or disagrees with them?
What is the outcome of a run whose backup succeeds and passes its check but whose status-file update fails?

quotes:
Each run writes its
   outcome and instant to a status file in the backup location, which a
   restart keeps; the owner interface shows the newest kept backup's instant
   and that last outcome, so the owner sees when a backup holds the import
   (A16 rule 10).

A backup and its check file are
   written under temporary names in the backup location — every one beginning
   with the prefix the release declares for them — and become a kept backup
   only when complete; at every start and every run Registry first removes
   every file left there under that prefix, and no other file.

A backup or a deletion that fails leaves no partial file, writes a
   diagnostic that names the failure and no value (A17), and is tried again at
   the next run; Registry keeps serving.
judgement.divergence: One implementation treats a completed checked backup as authoritative, reconstructs or repairs missing status metadata, and counts it for the day; another treats the status-file failure or inconsistency as a failed run, deletes or ignores the backup, and retries. The owner sees different status and retention results, and a later restore may use different backups.
judgement.why: The texts separately require a kept backup and a status-file update but do not define their atomic ordering, failure outcome, or restart reconciliation.

topics.topic: Required backup encryption construction and interoperable envelope format
questions: What exact cryptographic construction and authenticated backup format must implementations use?
What cryptographic format must every release use so backups are confidential, tamper-detecting and restorable across releases?
What cryptographic construction and backup envelope must every implementation use?

judgement.why: This is the same backup cryptographic construction and interoperable envelope-format question already assigned to State 6.

precedent.topic: Cryptographic algorithm, encoding, key handling, and authenticated format for backups
quotes: Each backup is encrypted with the backup key the configuration holds at its making (A17).
A backup cannot be read without the key it was made with.
precedent.why: The algorithm, nonce, authenticated envelope, key identifier and cryptographic-version representation are encoding and file-format contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Timing and durable tracking of the required post-import backup in owner-only mode
questions: If an import is accepted during an owner-only recovery start, is its backup attempted immediately or deferred until the next start with service tokens?
When an import is accepted during an owner-only start, is its backup attempted immediately or deferred until the next token-enabled start?
How does a restart know that the committed import still requires its special checked backup?

quotes:
The import answers once its transaction commits; right after it
   Registry makes a backup run outside the daily schedule (A18), so the import
   reaches a checked backup as soon as it can, and the owner interface shows
   when it has (A18 rule 1); a failed run is retried at the next run, and the import stays
   accepted.

A run that 03:00 found Registry stopped is made when
   it next starts with its service tokens, if no backup was made that UTC
   day; an owner-only start makes no run (rule 10).

An owner-only start makes no backup run, so no backup
holds the store before this is done; an import the owner repeats then
(R0-89) comes first, and its backup run is made at the next start with the
tokens.
judgement.why: A16 requires the special backup immediately after every accepted import, while A18 expressly defers an import repeated during an owner-only start until the next token-enabled start.

topics.topic: Accepted request-id syntax, length measurement, and equality
questions: What exact character repertoire and equality rule must a request id satisfy?
Exactly which request-id strings are accepted and how is the 128-character limit measured?

quotes:
'Create a project', 'record a customer', 'add a room' and 'publish an
   artifact pointer' each carry a request id: an opaque value the caller
   makes, unique for every create it means as new — printable text of at most
   128 characters, made from at least 16 random bytes, as a random UUID is; a
   blank one is missing (A02).
judgement.why: The exact character repertoire, string equality and measurement unit are field-format and encoding contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Ordering sign-out against concurrent session-state-changing requests
questions: May sign-out overlap an already validated request, or must it serialize behind every request that updates the session?

If sign-out is applied while an already-admitted request is showing a confirmation or uploading a file, may that request subsequently recreate state in the ended session, or must sign-out be ordered after it?

quotes:
Validity is
   checked when a request arrives (A04 rule 6, stage 1); a request that
   passes it completes even if a limit or a sign-out comes while it runs, and
   a restart that interrupts it leaves nothing of it (A04 rule 4).

The requests of one owner session that change its state — showing a
   confirmation step, uploading a file, a submission — are applied one at a
   time: each sees the session as the one before left it, so a confirmation
   bound to a file a later upload replaced is refused (A16 rule 2).
Everything in it ends with the session.
judgement.divergence: One implementation serializes sign-out after an admitted upload or confirmation request, allowing that request to finish and persist its session state first; another ends the session concurrently and discards or prevents the admitted request's later state update. The owner notices whether the upload or confirmation survives and can be used.
judgement.why: The texts guarantee completion after admission and serialize session-state changes, but do not place sign-out in that serialization or define whether completed work may recreate state after the session ends.

topics.topic: Owner-session cookie attributes and route, host, port, and HTTPS scope
questions: What exact cookie attributes and host/path rules enforce the intended scope, and may the cookie be sent to Registry's service-API routes on the same host?
What exact cookie Domain, Path, Secure and SameSite rules implement "Registry's own origin", especially when Registry shares a host with another port or is reached locally without HTTPS?

judgement.why: This is the same owner-session cookie attributes, host/path scope and HTTP transport question already assigned to State 6.

precedent.topic: Owner-session cookie scope, attributes, and HTTP behavior
quotes: The owner signs in with the owner credential (R0-30) and receives an owner session (M11), carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine (R0-29), and only to Registry's own origin.
precedent.why: Exact cookie attributes, host/path scope and SameSite transport policy are HTTP contract and encoding details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Valid service-token combinations for the owner-only configuration test
questions: Does the missing-Client-Portal test apply only when at least one service token is configured, or must a no-token configuration also fail?
Is a configuration with no Client Portal token valid when all four service tokens are absent, and what exact token combinations are valid?

quotes:
The configuration holds exactly these items and no other: the store's
   location; the backup location and the backup key (A18); the owner
   credential; one service token for each service of A09 — PresuPro, Client
   Portal, Cabinet, Cabinet Kernel (R0-20, R0-23) — or, for an owner-only
   start, none of the four: Registry then serves the owner interface alone
   and refuses every service call (A18 rule 10).

A configuration without Client Portal's token stops the start and names the
   missing item.
judgement.why: The normative rule permits a configuration with no Client Portal token when all four tokens are absent, while the required test unconditionally requires such a configuration to stop.

topics.topic: Whether CSRF protection applies to owner-interface reads
questions: Must an owner-interface read supply and pass the session's CSRF value, or is CSRF checked only for state-changing requests?
Must owner-interface reads carry and pass CSRF protection, or only state-changing requests?

quotes:
Every operation — read or change, of a service, Kernel or the owner —
   checks in one order, and the first failure is its answer; a stage that
   does not apply to it is skipped, and each check an operation states belongs
   to the stage of its kind: (1) the caller's authentication and its right to
   the operation (A09) — for the owner, a valid owner session, then its CSRF
   value, then a confirmation value where one is asked (A13);

Every change in the owner interface carries the CSRF protection bound to
   its session (R0-29); one from another session or none is refused.
judgement.why: A04 applies the owner CSRF check to every read or change, while A13 requires it only for changes.

topics.topic: Whether an import-triggered backup satisfies or suppresses the scheduled daily backup
questions: Does a checked post-import backup made earlier that UTC day satisfy or suppress that day's scheduled daily backup?
Does an import-triggered backup count as that day's daily backup, and if it occurs before 03:00 must the 03:00 daily backup still run?

quotes:
The import answers once its transaction commits; right after it
   Registry makes a backup run outside the daily schedule (A18), so the import
   reaches a checked backup as soon as it can, and the owner interface shows
   when it has (A18 rule 1); a failed run is retried at the next run, and the import stays
   accepted.

Registry backs up its store once a day at 03:00 UTC into the backup
   location, as a consistent copy taken while it runs: a backup never holds
   part of a transaction.

The run after an accepted import (A16)
   is made even when the day already has a backup, and keeps both; besides
   it, at most one backup is made per UTC day, the kept backups themselves
   saying which days have one, and runs never overlap.
judgement.why: The import-triggered run is expressly outside the daily schedule and additional to the one daily backup, so it does not suppress the scheduled run.

topics.topic: Definition of a request interrupted by restart
questions: What counts as an interrupted request: one whose transaction has not committed, or any request whose response was not completed before restart?

topics.topic: Ordering a repeated import relative to retention replay and audit cutoff recovery
questions: During recovery from a backup predating the import, must the repeated import occur before or after replaying retention actions and the audit cutoff?

topics.topic: Preserving and recovering the effective date of an ended relationship
questions: Which date does the recovery record preserve for an ended relationship, and how is the original effective end date recovered?

topics.topic: Request-id retry semantics after the originally created record is erased
questions: After a Project is anonymised/deleted or a Customer is erased, must the former request id still identify a retry, or may that retry create a second record?

topics.topic: Scope and precedence of confirmation validation checks
questions: Does stage 1 check only equality with the pending one-time value, or also its action, target, input and revision/access-version binding; and which failure is returned when that binding and a later check both fail?

topics.topic: Selecting the recovered audit cutoff after non-monotonic erasure dates
questions: Which cutoff is replayed when later audit-erasure actions used non-monotonic dates?

topics.topic: Time scope of the entry-existence equivalence invariant
questions: Is the equivalence meant only immediately after the action commits, or must it characterize the entries currently present after erasure and restore?

topics.topic: Whether an accepted import clears uploaded files in all owner sessions
questions: Does acceptance of any import drop uploaded files from all owner sessions, or only from the session that confirmed it?

topics.topic: Whether missing recovery evidence prevents leaving owner-only mode
questions: May the restored instance leave owner-only mode and serve services when the retention record or required export is missing, or must it remain owner-only until the missing evidence is corrected?
